faq.q: Which textbook do these Class 8 Sanskrit classes follow?

faq.q: Are the classes live or self-paced?

faq.q: Does it help with CBSE exams?

title: Sanskrit Alphabet Pronunciation Audio · Varṇamālā स्वर & व्यञ्जन Sounds | EdNet Learn
desc: Hear every letter of the Sanskrit alphabet: Varṇamālā pronunciation audio for vowels (स्वराः) and consonants (व्यञ्जनानि), grouped by place of articulation (स्थानम्), plus barakhadi.
intro: Sanskrit is a language of sound first. Our Varṇamālā (वर्णमाला) lets you tap any letter and hear it spoken clearly — every vowel (स्वर) and consonant (व्यञ्जन) — so you learn the right sound before you learn the shape.

Letters are grouped by where they are produced in the mouth (स्थानम्): throat, palate, roof, teeth and lips. Once that clicks, pronunciation becomes logical rather than memorised. Continue into the barakhadi (गुणिताक्षराणि) to hear consonant + vowel combinations.
gets: Tap-to-hear audio for every स्वर and व्यञ्जन
Sounds grouped by स्थानम् (place of articulation)
Barakhadi audio for consonant–vowel combinations
Tracing slate and Swar review quizzes
Pronunciation practice with feedback

faq.q: How many letters are in the Sanskrit alphabet?
faq.a: Traditional counts vary with how you treat ऌ, ॡ, anusvāra and visarga; our Varṇamālā shows all vowels and consonants with audio so you can hear each one.

faq.q: Why are letters grouped by mouth position?
faq.a: Sanskrit orders consonants by स्थानम् (place of articulation): कण्ठ्य, तालव्य, मूर्धन्य, दन्त्य, ओष्ठ्य. Learning the groups makes pronunciation systematic.
Yes, the Varṇamālā and Swar foundation pages are free to explore.

title: Learn Sanskrit Grammar Online · Vibhakti, Dhātu & Sandhi Step by Step | EdNet Learn
desc: Learn Sanskrit grammar online with interactive tools: vibhakti (case) tables, liṅga-vacana, numbers, dhātupāṭha verb forms and Pāṇinian explanations, from beginner to advanced.
intro: Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्) has a reputation for being hard. It is really a beautifully regular system — once you see the patterns. Our grammar hub teaches it the way a patient teacher would: one pattern at a time, with examples you can hear and play with.

Start with vibhakti (the eight cases), gender and number, then move to verbs through the Dhātupāṭha, where you can generate forms of any root and see how words are built. Everything is interactive and works in your browser.

faq.q: Can a complete beginner learn Sanskrit grammar online?
faq.a: Yes. Start with the Varṇamālā and vibhakti basics; each tool explains the pattern before asking you to use it.

title: Sanskrit Word Deconstructor Online · Break Words into Root, Syllables & Meaning | EdNet Learn
desc: Free Sanskrit word deconstructor online: type or paste a Devanagari word to see its syllables, conjunct consonants, transliteration and meaning, then trace verb forms back to the dhātu.
intro: Paste any Sanskrit word below and the deconstructor (पद-विश्लेषणम्) breaks it apart: syllables, conjunct consonants (संयुक्ताक्षराणि), transliteration and — when the word is in our dictionary — its meaning and part of speech.
For verbs, jump to the Dhātupāṭha deconstructor, which works backwards from a conjugated form to its root (धातु), tense and person.

faq.q: Can it find the root of a verb?
faq.a: Use the Dhātupāṭha deconstructor for verbs — it traces forms like गच्छति back to the root गम्.
